newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw, Ljubljana lead East European bourses slide.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw, Ljubljana lead East European bourses slide.

text.p: East and Central European shares lost ground this week with the Ljubljana and Warsaw bourses the worst affected of all the region's exchanges hit by profit-taking and slow busines.
The losses of blue chip stocks in Warsaw, Prague and Budapest pushed the Central European Share Index (CESI) down 2.1 percent to 1,442.97 points.
WARSAW

Polish shares fell this week and analysts said they could pick up next week but added it was difficult to say where the market, which lost 8.8 percent since recording a high on October 9 would find its support.

They said that though the overall economic situation remained positive the market seemed vulnerable to further profit-taking after breaking strong support at 14,000 points of the WIG index and falling to 13,745.6 on Thursday.
But some said generally positive economic climate and increased capital flows to emerging markets could push the WIG up to 16,000 points by year-end.
Analysts said Thursday's surprise parliament's decision to cut next year's lowest income tax levels was unlikely to affect the market since the taxes for top earners stayed unchanged.
But they said the political turmoil that arose after the decision could cause some investor concern.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian shares fell on profit-taking this week but traders expected the market to bottom out soon.
"Sooner or later the market will recoup but now investors are taking profits," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft. He saw the market's support at around 3,500 to 3,550 points.
On Thursday the BUX index closed at 3,604.99 points, down 102.46 from last Friday.

Traders saw the market rebounding in anticipation of an upgrade of Hungary's credit rating by Moody's and Standard & Poor's. They also expected the recent batch of macroeconomic data to have a positive impact.
PRAGUE
Financial sector gains halted the Prague Stock Exchange's October doldrums this week after reports that Nomura and ING bank were the top contenders to take a state-held stake in bank IPB.

But when the dust settled by mid-week, the bourse, which has recorded only two advancing sessions all month, was sliding again. The PX50 index closed on Thursday at 531.8, down 1.1 points on the week.

"If you bring in a foreign partner such as the... two banks mentioned, that addresses questions that have been hovering around IPB on its perceived lack of corporate structure and transparency," said Jay King of Wood and Company.
BUCHAREST
Sluggish business depressed prices, pushing two independent indices to year lows on Thursday, when turnover plunged to 20.5 million lei, or less than half the previous level.
Traders said buying interest was almost absent as investors prepared for the launch of an over-the-counter trading system.
BRATISLAVA
A need for fresh players and low market liquidity characterised another week of dull trading on the Bratislava bourse.
The 12-share SAX index hovered slightly above 200 points over the week, dipping to 201.91 points on Thursday's close, from 202.99 on Monday.
Brokers said investors seemed to have been waiting for main issues to fall before getting in.But traders said there was not much room for falls in shares such as VSZ, VUB, Nafta or Slovnaft.
ZAGREB
Croatian shares traded at lower prices throughout the week, with the fully listed issues seen as the only stocks able to hold out against the trend downwards.
The main losers were tourist firms which recorded spectacular gains in the previous weeks.
BULGARIA

No corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market for the second week in a row after the Bulgarian Securities and Stock Exchange Commission (SSEC) suspended stock trading on exchange floors until companies meet new legal requirements.

Under Bulgaria's stock trading law public companies had to submit by September 19 a detailed report on the size and distribution of their capital and a list of their shareholders to the SSEC for approval to be eligible for floor trading.
None of these companies has presented a report to the commission so far, the BSE said.
LJUBLJANA
Share prices fell 10.4 percent in Ljubljana. The SBI index fell 131.3 points to 1,136.9. Total turnover was 2.1 billion tolars ($15.2 million).
The biggest loser was health resort Terme Catez operator, which fell 15.8 percent.
